title: Waste Knights 2nd Edition - An Apocalyptic Adventure Worth Taking
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NHGisiXq7eg

Daniel (@dungeondive) unpacks Waste Knights 2nd Edition and finds, to his own surprise, the rarest thing in modern adventure gaming: a big Kickstarter that didn't stress him out. Everything fits in one base box — even all-in, with add-ons — and he compares the experience to walking into a game store a decade ago, buying something off the shelf, reading the rules and simply playing. The rulebook is well laid out with a good index, a chronicle sheet and a separate Kickstarter component guide.

What it actually is, he clarifies, is not the hex crawl the map implies. It's a scenario-driven hybrid of interactive gamebook and board game, splitting your time roughly evenly between the Book of Tales and the table. He praises the press-your-luck exploration deck — flip, evaluate the terrain, push again or take the final card — and reserves his strongest enthusiasm for the threat token system, which mutates the encounter cards drawn from a bag so no card plays the same way twice.

His main complaint is the railroading: strict scenario time limits mean he never feels free to wander the wasteland, and the base pledge is stingy with only three solo-playable scenarios. He liked it enough to late-pledge two expansions.

----

Waste Knights looks like a hex crawl but plays as a tightly scripted gamebook — does an adventure game owe you the freedom to wander, or is a time limit just honest pacing?
